resources.string: Weather layers and readouts for the map, and the user manual
Layers, forecasts, stations, buoys and gauges, page by page
Fire and hazmat weather for a point on the map, kept when the network drops
Fire weather stations from the National Interagency Fire Center (services3.arcgis.com). Red Flag colors use common national thresholds, not your local office\'s zone criteria.
Draw stations at this zoom or closer
Draw their readings at this zoom or closer

Atmosphere will ask the National Interagency Fire Center for the fire weather stations around you and what they are reading.

Unlike the other layers, this one sends a position: the point you measure from, rounded as far as your precision setting says. Switch it to Map center if you would rather it never send where you are.

Server: services3.arcgis.com
Draw gauges at this zoom or closer

Atmosphere will ask the National Water Prediction Service for the river gauges around you, what they read and what they forecast.

Like the weather stations, this one sends a position: a box around the point you measure from, rounded as far as your precision setting says. Switch it to Map center if you would rather it never send where you are.

Server: api.water.noaa.gov
Draw buoys at this zoom or closer

Atmosphere will ask the National Data Buoy Center for its latest observations: one file for the whole network, cut to the distance around you on the phone. A buoy\'s record also asks NOAA CO-OPS for the tide and current predictions at the nearest stations, by station id. Your position is not sent.\n\nServers: www.ndbc.noaa.gov, api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov
Buoys and coastal stations from the National Data Buoy Center (www.ndbc.noaa.gov)
River gauges and forecasts from the National Water Prediction Service (api.water.noaa.gov)
The last-3-days switch applies to the list too. Near me, on the map, by state or region: swipe on to the Spot forecasts page.
Show spot forecasts on the map?
Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service for the open spot forecast requests and draw them on the map. Your position is not sent. Server: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov
Here: outside the area being drawn
Show or hide this storm\'s maps
Hurricanes from the National Hurricane Center (%1$s)

Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service for the Storm Prediction Center\'s fire weather outlook areas for the next three days and draw them on the map. Your position is not sent. Server: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov
Fire weather outlook from the NOAA Storm Prediction Center (%1$s)

Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service for the Weather Prediction Center\'s excessive rainfall outlook areas for the next three days and draw them on the map. Your position is not sent. Server: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov
Excessive rainfall outlook from the NOAA Weather Prediction Center (%1$s)

Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service for the beach and surf zone forecast along the coast the map is showing and draw it on the map: rip current risk, surf and water temperature per beach. The map\'s area is sent; your position is not. Server: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov
Beach and surf zone forecast from the US National Weather Service (%1$s)

Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service for its daily snow depth analysis as a picture of the area the map is showing. The map\'s area is sent; your position is not. Server: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov
Snow analysis from the NOAA National Operational Hydrologic Remote Sensing Center (%1$s)

Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service\'s water prediction service for its picture of where its river model puts water over the banks, for the area the map is showing, now or at the worst of the next five days. The map\'s area is sent; your position is not. Server: maps.water.noaa.gov
Flood inundation from the NOAA National Water Prediction Service, experimental (%1$s)
The National Weather Service calls this experimental: a river model\'s estimate of where water goes over the banks, not a survey, and it covers only part of the country. What you can see wins.

Atmosphere will ask the National Weather Service\'s water prediction service which stretches of stream its river model has over their high-water mark in the area the map is showing, now or at the worst of the next five days, and draw them as colored lines. The map\'s area is sent; your position is not. Server: maps.water.noaa.gov
High-flow streams from the NOAA National Water Prediction Service, experimental (%1$s)
A line means the river model has that stretch over its high-water mark; the color is how rare a flow that big is. Experimental, and a computed flow, not a gauge reading. Tap a line for the numbers.
Atmosphere will ask NOAA\'s nowCOAST for the sea surface temperature analysis as a picture of the area the map is showing. The map\'s area is sent; your position is not. Server: nowcoast.noaa.gov
Sea surface temperature from NOAA nowCOAST (%1$s)

Atmosphere will ask the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service for its SNOTEL station list and the latest readings at the stations the map is showing: snow depth, snow water equivalent, temperature. The map\'s area is sent; your position is not. Server: wcc.sc.egov.usda.gov
SNOTEL readings from the USDA Natural Resources Conservation Service (%1$s)
Atmosphere will ask avalanche.org for every US avalanche center\'s forecast zones and today\'s danger ratings, and draw them on the map. Your position is not sent. Server: api.avalanche.org
Avalanche zones and danger ratings from the US avalanche centers via avalanche.org (%1$s)
Atmosphere will ask the National Hurricane Center which storms are running, and draw their forecast cones and tracks on the map. Your position is not sent. Server: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov
Show or hide this layer\'s settings
Radar from the US National Weather Service (%1$s)

Wind comes from the US National Weather Service, drawn as moving air over the map.

Turning it on lets Atmosphere ask them for wind over the part of the map you are looking at. Nothing else about you is sent.

Server: nomads.ncep.noaa.gov
Drawn for the middle of the map. Zoom in to see all of it.

Smoke comes from the US National Weather Service's forecast model, the same one the wind comes from: where the smoke is and how thick, near the ground or through the whole sky.

Turning it on lets Atmosphere ask them for smoke over the part of the map you are looking at. Nothing else about you is sent.

Server: nomads.ncep.noaa.gov
Here: outside the areas EPA has drawn
Air quality from the U.S. EPA\'s AirNow (%1$s)

Air quality comes from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's AirNow: the latest hour of ozone and fine particles, measured at monitors and drawn in the six Air Quality Index colors.

Turning it on lets Atmosphere ask EPA for the map of the whole country. Your position is not sent.

Server: services.arcgis.com
Every spot forecast request the National Weather Service has open, with the forecast they issued for each. Narrow it to near you, the map, a state or a region.
The National Weather Service takes spot requests on their own form and it cannot be filled in from here. Copy the point, open the form, then hold its USNG box, paste, and press Plot USNG.
Tap the map where the forecast is for

What you type goes to the US Census Bureau first, which answers with the street address or with nothing. If it has no answer, %1$s is asked \u2014 the address finder picked in ATAK\'s settings, which is also sent the area of the map on screen. You get to see what came back before it is used.
Copied %1$s \u2014 on the form, paste it into the USNG box and press Plot USNG
ATAK has no address search set up

Spot forecasts from the US National Weather Service (mapservices.weather.noaa.gov, api.weather.gov). Address search uses the US Census Bureau (geocoding.geo.census.gov), then the geocoder ATAK is set to.

Spot forecasts come from the US National Weather Service: the open requests from their spot forecast map service, and each forecast from their weather API.

Turning it on lets Atmosphere download the whole country's list and filter it on this phone. Your position is not sent.

Servers: mapservices.weather.noaa.gov, api.weather.gov

Radar comes from the US National Weather Service, the same picture their own radar site draws.

Turning it on lets Atmosphere ask them for radar over the part of the map you are looking at. Nothing else about you is sent.

Server: opengeo.ncep.noaa.gov
Tap the map to pick the point
